articles.title: España - Fiji en directo | Última hora de Mundial Sub-17 en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Por aquí cerramos este directo histórico. Hoy, con la goleada de España ante Fiyi (15-0) en la segunda jornada del Mundial Sub-17. Gracias por vivirlo
articles.body:
Última hora del España - Fiyi en directo:

¡¡¡Muuuy buenos días y bienvenidos a todos y todas a la segunda jornada de la fase de grupos del Mundial Sub-17 !!! España buscará seguir con las buenas sensaciones que dejó en el debut contra China , tras la gran victoria por 5-0 con goles de Pesquer, Tunkara, Trujillano y el doblete de Emeka .

El equipo dirigido por David Cubillo solventó el siempre complicado inicio de un torneo con dos goles al filo de la primera parte, para terminar sentenciando el encuentro en la recta final del partido. Las figuras de este primer choque fueron la perla del Barcelona , Ebrima Tunkara , que arrancó con un gol y asistencia , y el delantero del Granada , Owen Emeka , que perforó la portería rival por partida doble en apenas seis minutos .

La nota negativa es la baja del jugador del Athletic Club, Christian Imga , afectado de una lesión en los isquiotibiales que ya le tiene de vuelta en Bilbao y al que no se le podrá encontrar sustituto , debido a que el torneo ya ha comenzado . No obstante, Cubillo declaró que cuentan "con muchos jugadores polivalentes y harán que la baja de Imga no se note ".

Enfrente, un conjunto de Fiyi que se presenta como el conjunto más débil de un grupo con China y Marruecos . Precisamente, contra los africanos cayeron (6-0) en el primer partido del Mundial . La selección española buscará vencer por la máxima cantidad de goles posible antes de encontrarse con Marruecos el próximo jueves 26 de noviembre a las 16.00 horas, en caso de un empate en esa última jornada.

Desde las 13.30 horas, el combinado nacional Sub-17 seguirá su camino hacia la única estrella que le falta a la selección española con este enfrentamiento ante Fiyi, y te lo contaremos como siempre, aquí , en MARCA.

articles.title: Women's World Cup play-offs: Scotland v Sweden - Andreatta's preview
articles.summary: Scotland intend to bring fancied Sweden's World Cup dream "crashing down - and do it in a truly Scottish way", says manager Melissa Andreatta.
articles.body:
Scotland intend to bring fancied Sweden's World Cup dream "crashing down - and do it in a truly Scottish way", according to women's head coach Melissa Andreatta.

Scotland face a two-legged World Cup qualifying play-off against powerhouses Sweden, who are managed by Andreatta's former boss Tony Gustavsson.

The Swedes, who have been semi-finalists at the two previous Women's World Cups and are ranked eighth in the world, will be strong favourites to reach the tournament in Brazil next summer.

Andreatta, who has eight wins, two losses and four draws from her 14 games in charge of Scotland, was Gustavsson's deputy when he was Australia head coach from 2020 to 2024.

While the two have a connection from those years, the Australian is very much in business mode with next week's first leg at St Mirren Park looming.

"A few weeks ago Tony reached out, sent me a few messages and I took my time to respond," she told BBC Scotland.

"It wasn't much about football, just connecting on a personal level - which is probably a good thing, because I can be quite competitive. I just want to focus on business and not the personal level.

"I'm sure, like he is, all we're focused on is how we're going to win."

The Scots finished top of their qualifying group earlier this year after four wins from their six games before beating the Czech Republic 5-2 on aggregate in the play-off semi-final.

That set up the exacting play-off final against the Swedes, a team who narrowly missed out on a spot in the final at the previous two World Cups.

Scotland have made just one appearance at the tournament, in 2019, and Andreatta is excited by the prospect of getting one over her old boss for her new home.

"It's going to be a great occasion to face them at home first," she added.

"They are such a powerhouse nation that carries so much expectation to go to their next tournament. We want to bring that all crashing down and do that in a truly Scottish way. That's what we're going to focus on.

"I definitely won't be looking at their dug out, I'll be focused on us and what we need to do to get the result and go to another tournament.

"They are an exceptional team but we won't be swayed by a team's reputation or ranking.

"We firmly believe that anything is possible. Once that whistle goes, if you've done the work and you're prepared you're in the position to make anything happen. With this group of players and staff I know that's possible, we can take it to anyone on any given day.

"It is a massive challenge but we love those moments and that's why we're here. We've earned it."

Ayrshire beach helping Andreatta feel at home

There are more than 10,000 miles between Brisbane - where Andreatta grew up - and Ayr in Scotland, where she now calls home.

While the climate may be vastly different, there's one thing they do have in common - the beach.

"I love the coastal life. In Australia it's a big part of your lifestyle, being outdoors. I think there's something about the sea, being near it. Relaxing, calming, balancing," she said.

It has been 18 months since Andreatta was announced as Pedro Martinez Losa's successor as manager of the Scotland women's team and now, with her family alongside her - including two-year-old daughter Mackenzie - she feels at home.

"We've definitely settled in," she added. "We have the spots that we go to, our routine, we love it here. It's been a great landing spot for us on such a big move."

But what does her daughter make of her mum's job?

"She's got no idea," says Andreatta. "She just think's mum's on TV. Whenever she sees me she gets excited. Having her at the games is super special, being able to hold her on the pitch. She's such a joy.

"You do these things to make people proud and I want to make her proud."

Scotland without captain Weir for World Cup play-off

New strategy launched to transform Scottish women's football over 10 years

Andreatta was sitting in the pubs of Scotland over the summer as the Tartan Army headed over to the United States in their droves to watch the men's team compete at a first World Cup in almost 30 years.

The women won't have to wait that long if they can book a spot on the plane to Brazil next summer.

Andreatta is hoping to see just as many kilts on the Copacabana beach as there were in the bars of Boston.

"There is a strong desire among the group, not only players but also the staff, there is this desire to make their nation proud and show Scotland that the women's national team belongs here and deserves as much of the limelight as the men's," she added.

"Together we can make our nation proud and what better way to do it? To have our men at the World Cup and then the following summer our women.

"Watching from afar, what the fans did over there and in Boston, why can't we do that in Rio? That's what I'm envisaging but there's a lot to do and achieve before we get there."

articles.title: La 'masterclass' de Arbeloa: "Parecían Maldini y Baresi"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Fulham elogió la actuación de Bassey y Affenbruger en el 1-1 ante el Man. City
articles.summary: El técnico del Fulham elogió la actuación de Bassey y Affenbruger en el 1-1 ante el Man. City
articles.body: el pobre inicio del Fulham -tras seis jornadas marchaba colista con dos puntos de 18 posibles- le valió numerosas críticas a Álvaro Arbeloa. Los resultados no se correspondían con el buen juego desplegado por los 'cottagers'. Las victorias sobre los recién ascendidos Hull City (1-0) y Coventry City (0-1) sirvieron de punto de inflexión para un equipo que marcha decimoquinto, dos puntos por encima del descenso, pero que encadena ya cinco partidos sin perder en Premier: logró un meritorio punto en su visita al Aston Villa (1-1), igualó en casa frente al Newcastle (1-1) y logró un empate consagratorio en su visita al Manchester City (1-1). “Sabíamos que habíamos perdido nuestros últimos 20 partidos contra el Manchester City, pero les dije a los jugadores que, si jugábamos como nos gusta, tendríamos la oportunidad de vencerlos. Gané la última vez que estuve aquí, así que pensé que tendríamos la oportunidad de vencer al City. Creo que jugamos muy, muy bien y rendimos muy bien", subrayaba Arbeloa recordando la clasificación del Real Madrid para cuartos de la pasada Champions League. El gran éxito del Fulham fue reducir al City a su mínima expresión. Es, de hecho, el partido en lo que va de Premier que los pupilos de Enzo Maresca consiguieron generar menos ocasiones claras de gol (2). Un empate que deja otros dos grandes vencedores, además de Arbeloa: Calvin Bassey (Aosta, 1999) y David Affengruber (Schibbs, 2001). "Ahora mismo, es uno de los mejores centrales no sólo de la Premier League... sino del mundo", había advertido Arbeloa para referirse a Bassey. “Sentí que podíamos presionarlos muy bien si marcábamos a Haaland individualmente y David (Affengruber) y Calvin (Bassey), especialmente David, lo hicieron realmente muy bien contra él”, admitió el exentrenador del Real Madrid. Arbeloa fue un pasito más allá en sus elogios. "Les dije a Calvin y David que ahora son como Maldini y Baresi", comentó entre risas antes de proseguir con su análisis : "¡Qué pareja! Creo que lo hicieron muy, muy bien. Defendimos muy bien contra un equipo muy fuerte. Obviamente fue un trabajo de todos. Todos los jugadores hicieron un gran trabajo. Fuimos agresivos cuando teníamos que presionar y nos ayudamos unos a otros cuando tuvimos que defender en bloque bajo". Especialmente llamativo, en efecto, fue el partido de Affenbruger. El ex del Elche, fichado a cambio de 12 millones de euros en verano, ha ido 'in crescendo' con el paso de los partidos. En el Etihad fue, según 'Who Scored', el jugador del Fulham que más pases dio (58), que más despejes realizó (6), que más tiros bloqueó (3) y el segundo que más duelos aéreos ganó (4). "Mi primera acción fue un bloqueo contra Haaland. Cuando logras una acción exitosa contra un jugador tan fuerte, te da confianza. Y con tanta confianza en un partido como éste, todo es un poco más fácil", reconocía Affenbruger, elegido 'MVP': "Mi familia todavía no sabe que recibí el premio al 'Jugador del Partido'. Le enviaré una foto a mi hermano enseguida, se pondrá muy contento". Toda una 'masterclass'. Para el Fulham, con Maldini y Baresi, todo será más fácil.

articles.title: Indiana Out of CFB Playoff and 7 Other Overreactions after Week 12 of 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: From the very start, the 2026 college football season has been heavy on chaos. And for that, in this week of thanks, we are deeply appreciative.
articles.body:
From the very start, the 2026 college football season has been heavy on chaos. And for that, in this week of thanks, we are deeply appreciative.

On paper, Week 12 wasn't overflowing with influential games between Top 25 teams, although Saturday sent shockwaves through the sport that will carry well beyond the College Football Playoff bracket.

Indeed, the postseason bracket looks different than it did a week ago thanks to a slew of upsets that flipped the sport on its side. One unbeaten team lost, which means we have one remaining. And the defending national champions might find themselves on the outside looking in.

From the playoff to the Heisman to the hot seat, all elements are accounted for in this week's overreactions.

Indiana Will Miss the College Football Playoff

Let's start with a little disclaimer: more chaos is coming. And if you're Indiana, you better hope it arrives after losing 27-24 to Washington in overtime.

In many respects, this felt like a matter of time. The Hoosiers' offense has struggled for some time with multiple quarterbacks and the team nearly lost to Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan.

The College Football Playoff selection committee has made it clear it doesn't love this team's resume, ranking Indiana No. 8 last week despite having one loss. That was before this outcome. Things will obviously get worse.

Not helping matters is Indiana's out-of-conference scheduling, which consisted of North Texas, Howard and Western Kentucky.

We'll have a good idea on Tuesday night but expect the Hoosiers to drop significantly. It's a matter of how far. A remaining game against Purdue at home doesn't exactly help boost the resume whatsoever.

Maybe the right teams lose and Indiana will squeak in, although things suddenly look bleak. Stay tuned.

Beyond Indiana, the Big Ten Had a Disastrous Weekend

Consider this an extension of our thoughts on Indiana, although now we're broadening our focus.

It wasn't just the Hoosiers that imploded on Saturday. The conference as a whole had a nightmare weekend on all fronts.

UCLA lost its first game of the season to Michigan 18-16, and it might have lost more than that. Ty Dieffenbach, the team's starting quarterback already playing in place of the injured Nico Iamaleava, was carted off the field.

Needless to say, his immediate availability is in doubt.

Given how the CFB Playoff selection committee treated Florida State a few years ago, UCLA could be in serious trouble, especially with a loss to USC next week.

Elsewhere, Ohio State lost to Nebraska, which officially ended the Buckeyes' playoff chances. Ryan Day's team was hanging on by a thread, although that's over now.

Also, Ohio State is 7-6 in its last 13 games. Woof.

Penn State, while not in the playoff hunt, lost to Rutgers at home as roughly a three-and-a-half touchdown favorite.

While Matt Campbell seemed to be getting things back on track, well, this changes a lot. In fact, it's one of the worst losses of the season.

College Football's Overtime Rules Need a Drastic Overhaul

We get it. Ending a football game can be difficult.

But college football's current system is absolutely horrific, and it cannot be used if we're serious about filling the College Football Playoff with the best teams.

For those unclear, here is how it works.

Teams each get possession on the first drive at the 25-yard line. If the game is still tied, they start there again, although now there's a catch. If both teams score, they must each attempt a two-point conversion in the second OT.

From there, teams take turns going for what essentially amounts to two-point conversions until a winner is decided.

BYU and Kansas put the full scope of the rules on display this weekend, as did Michigan and UCLA.

Kansas failed the try, and then BYU got it. The Cougars kept their playoff hopes alive with a 31-29 win. The same situation happened for UCLA and Michigan. The Bruins failed on their try, and the Wolverines cashed in, beating UCLA 18-16.

Games cannot be decided with this format. The game is too long, too physical and too nuanced to be decided on a two-point conversion.

The teams deserve better. The sport deserves better.

We can do better. In fact, the sport's old rules were significantly better. In trying to progress, we've regressed.

We've clobbered plenty of other coaches for underwhelming performances this year, although we haven't spent much time on Texas A&M and Mike Elko.

To be clear, Elko won't—and shouldn't—be fired. The Aggies made the playoff a season ago, and we can't be that unreasonable.

That being said, the Aggies lost their fourth consecutive game on Saturday, falling to Oklahoma 28-7. Since beating Arkansas on October 3rd, Texas A&M has just one victory.

Simply put, it's been a woeful year, especially on the offensive side of the ball. Quarterback Marcel Reed has really struggled, and on Saturday, it was Brady Hart's turn to underwhelm.

Over the past three games, the Aggies have scored 23 points combined.

It doesn't get much better next week. Texas A&M plays Texas, and that doesn't bode well. While a rivalry game will get plenty of focus, let's be honest. This program is thinking about next year.

Considering how much this program has poured into its football team, 4-7 is not acceptable. One year will be reluctantly allowed, although a slow start next year could really spell trouble.

Dan Lanning Should Receive Coach of the Year Consideration

Sure, the strength of schedule isn't exactly daunting. If there's any knock to make about Oregon's four-game winning streak, this is it.

The Ducks have beaten Northwestern, Ohio State, Michigan and now Michigan State. While a few of those wins would have normally served as huge resume boosts, that's not the case.

Still, the efforts of late have been convincing. On Friday night, the Ducks left no doubt with a 45-7 win over Michigan State on the road. And over the past two weeks, Oregon has beaten both Michigan schools by a combined score of 76-14.

The Ducks' final regular-season game of the year will be played at home against Washington. A convincing win there, and it's incredibly likely this team will find a way into the playoff.

Given where this program was, it's nothing short of a miracle. Yes, the team has plenty of resources to help recruit players. This is not a Cinderella story by any means.

When you consider the loss of star quarterback Dante Moore and just how low this team got earlier in the year, Lanning deserves a ton of credit. Somehow, this team has found a way.

Time will tell how this team's resume stacks up compared to other bubble hopefuls, but one thing is clear. Oregon has played its way back into the conversation, and Lanning is a huge reason why.

Andrew Luck Will Bring Stanford Back to Prominence

The former Stanford quarterback dazzled in the NFL before his shocking early retirement, only to work his way back into the football world serving as his school's general manager.

It wasn't pretty early on this season for the Cardinal, although something shifted as the season progressed. Stanford won its sixth game of the season on Saturday, clobbering Cal 44-28.

After starting the season 2-4, Luck's team is 4-1 over its past five games. While we're not approaching anything close to what we saw at the program's peak under coach David Shaw, we're seeing a program that bottomed out finding its footing, and there's something incredibly satisfying in watching the process play out.

As for Luck, his fingerprints are all over this team. He's picked the coach, helped change the way the program approaches recruiting and is carving out a role other programs will soon copy.

Given the impact he had as a player, his second act at Stanford is one of the biggest stories the sport isn't talking about. At least not yet.

We spend so much time agonizing over the Heisman Trophy and the College Football Playoff that we sometimes forget about the greatest commodity in college football: joy.

There wasn't much of it in the Big Ten this week, although Lincoln, Nebraska was overflowing with it.

Nebraska fans have not experienced much of it in recent years, especially in games of substance. In fact, coming into Saturday the Cornhuskers had lost 31 consecutive games to ranked opponents.

Against Ohio State on Saturday, that streak came to an emphatic end.

Nebraska's 31-28 victory wasn't without some drama, and it wouldn't be a Cornhuskers game without some. Nebraska jumped out to a 14-point lead, although that lead evaporated early in the second half.

In the end, Matt Rhule's team found a way. It came against a reeling Ohio State team, although that part doesn't matter.

Think of the countless heartbreaks and squandered leads. Think of the pain this fanbase has felt. While it might not put this team in the playoff, it doesn't matter.

Nebraska fans, enjoy this one. Goodness, you have earned it.

The Group of Six Playoff Suddenly Has Drama

Deep in the night on Saturday, Boise State uncorked a monumental collapse against San Diego State that could have a massive impact on the postseason.

We could spend plenty of words talking about the decisions made by Spencer Danielson and his staff regarding clock management and play-calling. Needless to say, the Broncos gave away the game, losing 22-20.

Now, however, things are getting interesting.

We assumed Boise State was bound for the College Football Playoff, with one Group of Six team set to make the bracket. This loss unquestionably halts that momentum.

Boise State plays Colorado State next week and then faces San Diego State once again in the Pac-12 Championship Game.

Teams like Liberty (10-1), New Mexico (9-2) and UTSA (9-2) are suddenly very much in the mix with games still to be played. We'll see what the selection committee has to say, although we're far from done.

articles.title: Thibaut Courtois: "Si queremos luchar por todos los títulos, necesitamos al mejor Vinicius"
articles.standfirst: El guardameta del Real Madrid habló en la previa del duelo de Champions ante el PSV
articles.summary: El guardameta del Real Madrid habló en la previa del duelo de Champions ante el PSV
articles.body: Thibaut Courtois compareció en la víspera del duelo frente al PSV y dejó un mensaje de plena confianza en el crecimiento del Real Madrid. El guardameta belga destacó la evolución del equipo en las últimas semanas y señaló como momento clave la reacción mostrada tras el descanso del encuentro ante el Celta, una transformación que atribuyó en gran parte a la intervención de José Mourinho. "Lo que hizo este pasado partido contra el Celta", destacó Courtois al referirse al técnico portugués, cuya charla en el intermedio considera fundamental para cambiar la dinámica del encuentro. El guardameta explicó que el equipo viene mostrando una mejora progresiva desde el inicio de la temporada y que la remontada lograda en Roma supuso el impulso definitivo para dar ese paso adelante. "Ante el Betis no merecimos perder y contra el Atlético tendríamos que haber creído más en nosotros mismos", reflexionó el internacional belga, que considera que el grupo comprende cada vez mejor las ideas de Mourinho. "La remontada en Roma nos dio ese plus. Ese partido fue fundamental para ese clic". Courtois también elogió la evolución del entrenador portugués, al que conoce desde los 22 años. "Creo que tiene más experiencia. Con los años se cambia. Ahora quizás se toma las cosas con más tranquilidad. Con el equipo es tranquilo pero cuando tiene que hablar, habla claro", afirmó. En lo personal, el guardameta no ocultó su deseo de seguir ligado al club blanco durante muchos años. "Mi objetivo es terminar mi carrera aquí", aseguró. Además, destacó la dificultad añadida que supone el nuevo formato de la Champions League, aunque insistió en que la ambición del equipo sigue siendo máxima: "El objetivo es ganar más". Uno de los nombres propios de la comparecencia fue Vinicius. Courtois salió en defensa del brasileño en un momento en el que las críticas vuelven a acompañar algunas de sus actuaciones. "Todos nos arropamos. A cualquier jugador le ayudaremos", aseguró antes de recordar que el nivel de excelencia permanente solo estuvo al alcance de leyendas como Messi o Cristiano Ronaldo. "Si queremos luchar por todo, necesitamos al mejor Vini". El belga también se mostró comprensivo con los silbidos que en ocasiones aparecen en el Santiago Bernabéu. "El aficionado paga mucho dinero para vernos. Tiene su derecho", afirmó. Aunque admitió que los pitos no siempre ayudan, recalcó que la enorme exigencia del madridismo es una de las señas de identidad del club. Sobre su papel bajo palos, Courtois dejó una reflexión que provocó sonrisas en la sala de prensa. "Hay veces que no son paradas. Me ven ahí y les impongo, y ellos fallan", comentó, reivindicando la influencia psicológica que puede ejercer un portero sobre los delanteros rivales. Por último, el guardameta volvió a pronunciarse sobre el Balón de Oro y lamentó la dificultad que tienen los porteros para competir por el galardón. Recordó que Manuel Neuer estuvo cerca de conseguirlo y reconoció que en 2022 esperaba una mejor clasificación, aunque entendió la victoria de Karim Benzema. "No sé qué temporada tendría que hacer un portero para lograrlo", confesó. "Con un equipo con Arda, Jude, Kylian o Vini, ¿cómo me van a votar a mí?", explicó el belga, que concluyó su intervención con elogios para Carlos Espí y Jude Bellingham.

articles.title: El recambio a Lamine Yamal: Jesse Bisiwu, la apuesta de futuro millonaria del Barça para la delantera
articles.standfirst: Primera citación del belga con Flick: está en la lisa de Champions contra el Sabah
articles.summary: Primera citación del belga con Flick: está en la lisa de Champions contra el Sabah
articles.body: El Barça viaja este lunes a Azerbaiyán para disputar el miércoles el quinto encuentro de la fase de la liguilla de la Champions League contra el Sabah. Hansi Flick tiene importantes bajas para este cruce continental, supone el viaje más largo que haya realizado nunca el bloque culé en competiciones europeas (Bakú está a 3.970 kilómetros de Barcelona), entre las que destaca la de Lamine Yamal, y para amortiguar las ausencias, el técnico germano recurre nuevamente al fútbol base azulgrana. En esta ocasión, la gran novedad es Jesse Bisiwu, la millonaria apuesta de futuro de la entidad catalana para su delantera. El joven atacante belga, de 18 años, llegó al Barça el pasado verano a cambio de 8,5 millones de euros. Bisiwu, que se estrena en una convocatoria del primer equipo, empezó a dar sus primeros toques al balón en el Lovaina, en el año 2014, institución en la que militó hasta 2020, cuando dio el salto al Brujas, entidad del que lo ficha el Barcelona el pasado 31 de julio. En 2023, cuando todavía tenía 15 años, comenzó a competir con el filial, el Club NXT, con el que disputó 36 partidos en la Segunda División de Bélgica. Bisiwu, que es internacional sub 21, ha pasado por todas las categorías inferiores de Bélgica y destacó en el Europeo sub 17 de 2025 (fue elegido en el once ideal del torneo), puede jugar en los dos extremos (es diestro) y desde que llegó al Barça Atlètic ha ido alternando su trabajo en el bloque de Belletti con algunas sesiones con el primer equipo culé. Ha participado en ocho encuentros en Segunda Federación (los ocho de titular), en los que ha dado una asistencia. Flick le ha seguido muy de cerca desde que llegó a la Ciudad Deportiva, fue uno de los jóvenes a los que llevó de pretemporada y deslumbró, por ejemplo, con un doblete contra el Basilea. El preparador germano ha ido tomando, estos meses, muy buena nota de sus cualidades: sobresale por su velocidad, habilidad en el regate, talento para el desborde y el uno contra uno, capacidad de asociación, disparo, potencia... y de ahí su convocatoria de hoy para el cruce de la quinta jornada de la fase de la liguilla de Champions League contra el Sabah. La citación de Bisiwu, con contrato en el Barça hasta junio de 2031, responde a la baja de Lamine Yamal, que se ha quedado en la Ciudad Condal a causa de unas molestias en el tobillo derecho, que no le impedirán estar el domingo contra el Dépor: no juega contra el Sabah por precaución. También se quedan en Barcelona los lesionados Rodri, Xavi Espart, Christensen, Hamza Abdelkarim y Bardghji.

articles.title: Mourinho y el calendario: "Es un conflicto, pero al final es el plin plin"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador portugués analizó el partido frente al PSV en Valdebebas
articles.summary: El entrenador portugués analizó el partido frente al PSV en Valdebebas
articles.body: Las lesiones de Harry Kane y Désiré Doué vuelven a poner el foco en un calendario cada vez más exigente y en el debate sobre los límites físicos de los futbolistas. José Mourinho abordó esta cuestión en rueda de prensa con un discurso que no esquivó la realidad económica del fútbol. "Creo que si queremos pasta, tenemos que trabajar mucho, tenemos que correr riesgos y es la vida. Si algún jugador quiere hacer huelga porque jugamos mucho, se le puede proponer que gane un 50% menos. Es un conflicto, pero al final es el plin plin (gesto de dinero con la mano y risas). Pero si me dan la opción de jugar solo cada tres días sería mejor", aseguró. Aunque él lo tiene claro: "Yo no me bajaría el sueldo (risas). Mismas ruedas, mismo sueldo", bromeó. Finales complicados: "Depende de la situación, a veces ganar en el último minuto tiene muchas cosas buenas, tiene sus riesgos. En los últimos 15 minutos, el riesgo estaba ahí, cuando arriesgas y cambias el perfil y vas a por todo, abres la puerta a que puedas tener algún contratiempo y no sacar ni un punto. Y puedes perder. La situación perfecta es un partido como Valencia, como Santander. Llegas y en cinco minutos sabes cómo terminará el partido. Hay otras en las que no eres capaz. Dije que el Celta tenía mucha culpa, positiva, del partido tan complicado. La situación de viajes, de no entrenar, de estar juntos por primera vez el día antes... Por suerte tengo a buenos mentirosos, los que me dicen que están a tope para jugar, y no lo están. Me encantan, pero me dicen que están a tope y no lo están. Con esos factores hay una situación límite. Piensas que es fantástico, pero si pensamos en los últimos minutos, más descuento, jugando con Arda y Jude, muertos los dos, y todos jugando con mucha mentalidad... Son condiciones en condiciones normales no los ganas. Son puntos de oro. Crédito para todos, también para los mentirosos que lo han dado todo". Vinicius: "Yo creo que volverá a su potencial máximo. Es joven y a veces los jugadores cuando se acercan a los 30... algunos de ellos no consiguen mantener el nivel físico ideal. Algunos también pierden la motivación... pero Vini es joven, la gente se olvida de que ha llegado aquí muy joven, que ha ganado todo...pero como decía cuando lo querían matar, es muy buen chico, muy empático con todos y esto es una base fundamental. Ha llegado, participación muy positiva. Contra el Villarreal cambia el partido, hace un gol... y después su gol es anulado y está cuatro partidos fuera. Quizás se ha interrumpido un momento de crecimiento, de confianza, condición y quizás se ha interrumpido con esa expulsión". Reflexión sobre el fútbol: "La diferencia es que en uestras generaciones para parecer tenías que ser... y ahora hay muchos que parecen antes de ser y otros que parecen sin nunca llegar a ser. Es una diferencia fundamental. Más que el fútbol haya cambiado, las herramientas y la dimensión de los staffs, los datos... todo lo que tienes para controlar las cargas, etc. El mundo ha cambiado y te tienes que adaptar". Palabras de Comesaña tras la derrota frente al Barça: "Tiene amnesia, contra el Real Madrid: 2-0, partido acabado, Vinicius expulsado... Tiene amnesia. O entonces lo que hace es meter a los dos en el mismo saco. Que lo haga, pero con Negreira que no nos meta en el mismo saco". ¿Algún jugador con manera de entrenador?: "No sé, conversaciones sobre fútbol siempre tienes... sobre nuestro fútbol y nuestras cosas. Me gusta que el jugador está consciente y confortable con lo que pedimos. Pensar en jugadores que algún día puede ser es complicado porque tenemos mucha gente joven. Bernardo Silva yo creo que será presidente del Benfica, pero de jugadores me cuesta pensar ahora". Partido ante el PSV: "Es un buen equipo, uno que vale más que los puntos que tiene. Vienen aquí a por los puntos, no vienen a pensar que vienen a perder. Grandes jugadores, entrenador con mucha experiencia... no es un partido fácil para nada. Tres días entre partido bien, pero dos es duro. Ellos también han jugado como nosotros, el sábado. Obviamente un partido que tenían ganado al minuto 60. Como siempre hago, un par de piernas frescas con energía cuando hay poco tiempo entre partidos. Los 12 puntos nos dan la tranquilidad... pero hay que seguir que no queremos jugar el playoff". Análisis del rival: "Es buena pregunta, pero no debería darte detalles. Debo proteger las sensaciones que tengo. Pero claramente tienen una identidad. Lo tienen a nivel defensivo y con la pelota. Y no sorprende que tengan a un entrenador que lleva varios años en el club. Es algo que valoro mucho. Tienen algunos jugadores con experiencia, como Kostic, Perisic... Y a jóvenes con calidad. Será complicado, para todos".

articles.title: Chaos in Italy: Footballer shown red card reportedly returns to pitch with knife and grabs rival official by the throat, forcing match abandonment
articles.summary: In a shocking incident during a Sicilian amateur football match, a red-carded player returned with a knife, forcing the game to be abandoned and prompting an investigation by police and the Italian Football Federation.
articles.body: A red card is usually the end of a player's involvement in a football match. In an amateur fixture in Sicily, however, a dismissed player returned from the dressing room carrying a knife, turning an already heated confrontation into an incident that brought the game to a permanent halt and prompted a police investigation.Red card after player allegedly kicks opponentThe incident took place on Sunday, November 22, at the Polisportivo Strasatti, on Via Brugnone in Marsala, during a Terza Categoria fixture between home side Galactic Paolini and Athletic Partanna.The match was part of the fourth round of the first half of the Trapani Third Category championship. Referee Vincenzo Pernice was in charge of the contest, which never reached the final whistle.According to an account published by Athletic Partanna on its official channels, tensions first developed when Paolini's No. 10 repeatedly directed insults towards the visiting team's bench. The situation escalated following an on-field confrontation, when the same player allegedly kicked a Partanna footballer several times while play was stopped.Pernice intervened and showed the Paolini player a straight red card. Athletic Partanna coach Calandra was also dismissed after stepping in to defend his player and provide assistance.The incident might have ended with those dismissals, but the situation became considerably more serious when the home player returned from the dressing room.Sent-off player returns carrying a knifeAccording to the account from Athletic Partanna, the dismissed player came back onto the pitch carrying a folding knife, described in reports by La Sicilia and la Repubblica as a switchblade.The club's management said he threatened the visiting coach, several officials and multiple Partanna players. The most alarming moment came when he allegedly grabbed one of the visiting club's officials by the throat while holding the knife in his other hand.The confrontation ended without anyone suffering physical injuries, but the presence of a weapon made it impossible for the match to continue safely. Pernice therefore abandoned the fixture permanently.Athletic Partanna's vice-president called the police, while emergency services were also contacted through Italy's 112 emergency number. Officers arrived at the sports facility, identified those present and collected initial statements from witnesses before opening an investigation.Athletic Partanna to report incident to FIGC and judiciaryAthletic Partanna has announced that it intends to take formal action to protect its players, coach and officials, reporting the incident to both the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) and the judiciary.The abandoned fixture will now be subject to review by the sporting authorities, who will consider the referee's report before deciding its official outcome and any disciplinary measures. articles.title: Match Officials: István Kovács to referee Manchester City vs Napoli (UEFA Champions League)
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca's side continued where they had largely left off prior to the final international break of 2026, failing to win once again in the Premier League...
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca's side continued where they had largely left off prior to the final international break of 2026, failing to win once again in the Premier League - the fourth time in a row in the competition.

Adding to three successive defeats, Manchester City were held by Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon as Elliot Anderson's volley in the second-half cancelled out Rodrigo Muniz's opener.

City now find themselves six points behind league leaders and reigning champions Arsenal in the English top-flight, sitting in third place behind Brighton & Hove Albion going into Sunday's meeting with the Gunners at the Emirates Stadium.

Before then is an equally as testing encounter for Manchester City to try and improve their confidence and run of form as they take on Massimiliano Allegri's Napoli in the league phase of the Champions League.

It is another return to the Etihad Stadium for Kevin De Bruyne after his homecoming with the Naples club last campaign - an encounter that saw the Belgian withdrawn early via a substitution in light of a red card for the Italian giants.

Now, ahead of the meeting between Manchester City and Napoli, UEFA have announced the list of match officials to oversee proceedings at the Etihad Stadium!

UEFA have confirmed that Romanian match official István Kovács will lead the team of referees overseeing proceedings between Manchester City and Napoli in the Champions League this week.

The 42-year-old referee from Carei will be taking charge of his 13th match across all competitions at the Etihad Stadium, having so far issued 60 yellow cards, eight second yellow card dismissals, four straight red cards, and awarding seven penalties in the process.

This will be Kovacs' second outing in the UEFA Champions League this campaign too, having officiated Real Madrid's 4-1 win over RB Leipzig - who lost 2-3 to Manchester City in the league phase - at the Bernabeu in late October.

Manchester City have a strong record in matches officiated by the Romanian referee, winning three of the four such matches, but losing the last such clash in a 3-1 defeat to Real Madrid in the last-16 play-offs of the Champions League in February 2025.

City's other results in games overseen by Istvan Kovacs are a 4-3 win over Real Madrid in late April 2022, a 1-0 win over Atletico Madrid in early April 2022, and a 1-5 away win at Club Brugge in October 2021.

Joining Istvan Kovacs on the pitch at the Etihad Stadium will be fellow Romanian referees Mihai Marica and Ferencz Tunyogi , UEFA have confirmed, appointed into the roles of assistant referees for the match.

Overseeing Manchester City against Napoli from the VAR Hub will be Poland's Tomasz Kwiatkowski as Video Assistant Referee, seated alongside the Netherlands' Dennis Higler as Assistant Video Assistant Referee.

Standing between the two dugouts for Manchester City against Napoli, and completing an all-Romanian team of match officials for the clash will be Florin Andrei , UEFA have confirmed.

articles.title: Watch: Argentina star Leandro Paredes collapses during live TV interview moments after captaining Boca Juniors to Copa Sudamericana glory
articles.summary: Leandro Paredes collapses during a live TV interview shortly after captaining Boca Juniors to Copa Sudamericana victory, showcasing the intense conditions of the match and his remarkable recovery.
articles.body: Leandro Paredes had barely finished celebrating Boca Juniors’ latest continental triumph when the celebrations took an unexpected turn. The Argentina international, who had already been forced off during the final because of the conditions in Barranquilla, fainted while speaking to a television reporter moments after the 2-0 victory over Atlético Mineiro.Paredes collapses during television interview after finalBoca Juniors captain Paredes, 32, started Saturday’s Copa Sudamericana final against Brazilian side Atlético Mineiro, but struggled with the heat and humidity at the venue in Barranquilla, Colombia. The heat index reportedly approached 40 degrees Celsius during the match, with forecasts before kick-off pointing to temperatures of around 32C and humidity close to 80%.The midfielder asked to be substituted and left the field in the 58th minute. He had already spoken to ESPN Argentina after the match, discussing his desire to compete and win, before fainting during a separate interview with DSports.Videos showed a reporter attempting to break his fall as he collapsed. Paredes regained consciousness, received medical attention and was able to walk back to the Boca dressing room, where he rejoined his teammates' celebrations. He was subsequently taken to a medical facility and given an intravenous drip.Boca manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena said he had noticed the midfielder struggling before his substitution.“He felt dizzy towards the end of the first half,” Arruabarrena said.“He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second half you could see he was struggling.”Paredes reassures supporters after health scareBoca later shared a video of Paredes returning to the team's hotel, accompanied by a message intended to reassure supporters.“Leandro Paredes feeling a bit dizzy from all the spinning around -- everything's all good over here,” the club wrote.Paredes also addressed the incident on Instagram, thanking fans for their messages and playing down the episode.“We're champions @bocajrs. Thanks to everyone for the messages -- it was just a bit of dizziness from all those laps together,” he wrote.Boca decided to remain in Barranquilla overnight following the incident before travelling back to Buenos Aires on Sunday afternoon. Paredes appeared in good spirits as he stepped off the plane, proudly holding the Copa Sudamericana trophy.Boca end 18-year wait for international silverwareThe victory over Atlético Mineiro gave Boca Juniors their first international trophy in 18 years and their 19th continental or international cup. It also moved the Argentine club ahead of domestic rivals Independiente, who have 18, to become South America's most decorated club in international competitions since 1960.For Paredes, the triumph carried particular significance. The midfielder began his professional career at Boca before moving to Europe in 2015, later representing clubs including Paris Saint-Germain and returning to the Argentine side.He was part of Argentina's squad that won the 2022 FIFA World Cup and also featured in the country's 2026 campaign, in which Argentina finished as runners-up to Spain. Paredes wore the No. 5 shirt in both tournaments.His 2026 World Cup campaign was followed by disciplinary action from FIFA. After the final against Spain in July, Paredes was involved in an on-field altercation with Spanish players Eric García and Gavi. FIFA subsequently handed him a 10-match international suspension and a $90,000 fine in August, ruling him out of Argentina's subsequent international fixtures.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bold predictions for Monday Night Football in NFL Week 11
articles.summary: Bold predictions for MNF in Week 11 between the Commanders and Bengals.
articles.body:
NFL Week 11 Monday Night Football features the Cincinnati Bengals visiting the Washington Commanders. The Bengals and Commanders are both in the hunt for their respective divisions. However, Cincinnati is leading the AFC North while Washington is chasing 1 st –place New York and 2 nd –place Dallas in the NFC East.

Along with Cincinnati leading the AFC North, quarterback Joe Burrow is having one of the best seasons of his career, leading the league in completion percentage, touchdown passes, and quarterback rating. He slightly trails Green Bay's Jordan Love for the most passing yards in the NFL.

Only time will tell if Washington is up for the tough task of stopping one of the league's hottest offenses. Entering Monday Night Football, here are four bold predictions.

Bengals running back Chase Brown will have a new career milestone

Monday night's game has Chase Brown's name written all over it. Brown will face off against a Washington defense allowing the 9 th –most yards per game. The running back will be a key contributor in both running and passing situations. This will be the best game of his season and career.

Prediction: Chase Brown will have a career day against the Commanders, reaching 100 yards rushing, 100 yards receiving, and finding the end zone three times. All three achievements are career firsts.

Cincinnati tight end Mike Gesicki will end Monday Night Football leading the position in touchdown receptions

Mike Gesicki is having one of the best seasons of his career. He enters Monday night tied with the most touchdown receptions of any previous season. Among tight ends, Gesicki is 2nd in touchdowns and has had a five-game stretch of finding the end zone. He will be a focus against a Washington defense allowing the 4 th –most receptions, 2 nd –most yards, and 2 nd –most touchdowns to opposing tight ends.

Prediction: Joe Burrow will connect with Mike Gesicki for two touchdowns on Monday Night Football, and Gesicki will move into first place, among tight ends, in touchdown receptions.

Washington will have more rushing yards than any other game this season

The Commanders have underperformed this season. The defense has taken a giant leap backward, and the offense is mediocre. Monday night's game can get out of hand if Washington allows Cincinnati to possess the ball for an extended period. That said, Washington will extend drives by efficiently running the football.

Prediction: The Commanders will run the football throughout the night, reaching 250 yards rushing for the first time this season.

Washington tight end Chig Okonkwo will catch his first touchdown of the season

Okonkwo's first season with Washington hasn't gotten off to a great start. However, Week 11's matchup with Cincinnati favors the veteran tight end. The Bengals' defense has allowed the 6 th –most receptions and 3 rd –most receiving yards to opposing tight ends. As the Commanders find success on the ground, Okonkwo will be left open in passing situations.

Prediction: Chig Okonkwo will have his best game of the season, reaching a new season-high in yards receiving and catching his first touchdown pass.

articles.title: Packers vs. Rams: 3 key matchups to watch in Week 12
articles.summary: Highlighting three important matchups for the Packers in Week 12 against the Rams.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers will be back on the road coming out of their bye week to face the Los Angeles Rams in the NFL's first-ever game on Thanksgiving Eve.

This will be a crucial game for both teams in terms of playoff seeding. Green Bay sits at 6-4 and is the current No. 7 seed, but a loss on Wednesday would hurt its postseason chances. Los Angeles is also 6-4 but on the outside of the current playoff picture as the No. 9 seed. The Rams' struggles have been surprising coming off a season where they reached the conference championship and then used the offseason to acquire Myles Garrett and talk Aaron Donald out of retirement for another Super Bowl run.

Even though both teams aren't where they hoped to be after entering the year with high expectations, they have done a good job navigating injuries to keep their seasons alive heading into Week 12.

Riding a four-game win streak, the Rams are the hotter team. Meanwhile, the Packers are coming off a crushing 30-10 loss to the Vikings and can't afford many more losses.

Here are three key matchups to keep an eye on this tense NFC showdown:

Packers run defense vs. Rams RBs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum

With Puka Nacua out for the season and Davante Adams set to miss another week, expect the Rams to lean on their eighth-ranked rushing attack in yards per game.

Los Angeles tends to ride the hot hand, and lately, that's been Corum, who leads the team in rushing yards over the past three games. That said, Williams is still leading the Rams' backfield in attempts, yards, and touchdowns.

Green Bay is surrendering 149.3 rushing yards in losses this season, so limiting Corum and Williams will be crucial. Unfortunately, they can't be sure how Los Angeles will deploy its two-headed backfield, so they'd better have a plan to deal with both.

Packers OTs Jordan Morgan and Anthony Belton vs. Rams edge rushers Myles Garrett and Byron Young

How much time will Jordan Love have to throw on Wednesday? The answer could come down to how the Packers' offensive tackles fare against the Rams' edge rushers.

In his first season as the full-time left tackle, Morgan has allowed a team-high five sacks but has the highest pass-blocking grade among Green Bay's starting offensive linemen, according to Pro Football Focus. Filling in for Zach Bako-Bewele, Belton has allowed two sacks but leads the team in allowed pressures with 25.

The offense needs strong performances out of both Morgan and Belton this week. Garrett is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and a potential game-wrecker, while Young is one of the league's best young pass rushers, leading the Rams in sacks (5.5) and pressures (40).

Morgan wore a cast on his left hand during Saturday's practice, so it will be interesting to see how that affects him.

Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons vs. Rams OT Warren McClendon Jr.

All signs point toward Parsons making his season debut in Week 12. On Sunday, he practiced in pads for the first time since last year's season-ending knee injury.

Parsons is one of the few players who can rival Los Angeles' Garrett in terms of impact. In 14 games last season, he racked up 12.5 sacks and 79 pressures, earning his fourth All-Pro selection.

It's anyone's guess how many snaps Parsons will play in his first game back, but when he is on the field, most of his snaps may come against McClendon. The Rams' right tackle has had some tough moments this year. In their Week 3 loss to the Broncos, he allowed a season-high seven pressures, had two penalties, and gave up a sack to Zach Allen.

The Packers' defense has arguably looked championship-caliber at times this season, and that's without their best player. Now, Parsons appears ready to return and has a favorable matchup right out of the gate.

articles.title: El Mundial es cosa de niños
articles.standfirst: España se divierte con un festival de goles ante Fiyi (15-0) en su segundo partido del Mundial Sub-17 e iguala su récord goleador histórico
articles.summary: España se divierte con un festival de goles ante Fiyi (15-0) en su segundo partido del Mundial Sub-17 e iguala su récord goleador histórico
articles.body: A las 15.30 horas en Doha, el reloj marcaba el momento del recreo para España. Y los 'niños' de David Cubillo se lo pasaron de miedo ante Fiyi (goleadores...) Un festival sin descanso. Una exhibición de fútbol ofensivo que convirtió el campo cuatro del Aspire Zone en el patio de colegio de una generación que.... Era momento de rotar. De repartir esfuerzos. De descubrir nuevas caras. Cubillo agitó el once y dio entrada a futbolistas que todavía no habían disfrutado de su estreno mundialista. Darlington se colocó bajo palos, Baba ocupó el lateral izquierdo y Raúl Expósito hizo lo propio en el carril contrario. Apenas tres supervivientes respecto al equipo que goleó a China: Marco Company, Holmes Júnior y Roberto Tomás. España afrontaba su segundo asalto con los dieciseisavos en el horizonte, pendiente también de lo que sucediera entre Marruecos y China. Enfrente, Fiyi. La 'cenicienta' del grupo. Dos selecciones separadas por más de 17.500 kilómetros. Una distancia geográfica inmensa, pero todavía menor que el abismo futbolístico que las separaba. Porque España apenas necesitó cinco minutos para empezar a divertirse. Rafa Cruz recibió abierto en la izquierda, se deshizo de su marcador con un solo toque y dibujó un disparo bombeado que superó al guardameta. Un golazo para abrir la lata. Y una celebración que tuvo un destinatario especial. Los internacionales corrieron hacia el banquillo para recoger la camiseta de Christian Imga, obligado a abandonar la concentración por una lesión muscular. El primer gol fue para él. Una dedicatoria que convirtió la alegría del estreno en un homenaje al compañero ausente. Y apenas hubo tiempo para respirar. En el minuto nueve, Ïu Martínez apareció por la derecha, Trujillano descargó de primeras desde la frontal y Rafa Cruz irrumpió en el área para firmar el segundo. Dos llegadas. Dos goles. España había encontrado una autopista hacia la portería rival y no pensaba levantar el pie. El tercero cayó acto seguido. Otra vez Iu por la derecha, otro desajuste de la defensa fiyiana y un balón suelto que Roberto Tomás aprovechó para superar al portero con un disparo por encima de su cabeza. La superioridad española era absoluta. Cada ataque parecía esconder una ocasión. Cada ocasión, una amenaza de gol. Fiyi encontró entonces una tregua. Breve. Casi testimonial. Ocho minutos después, Roberto Tomás volvió a aparecer para culminar una combinación tejida desde la derecha y firmar su segundo tanto. Pero la tranquilidad del conjunto del Pacífico duró exactamente lo que tardó en sacar de centro. España recuperó la pelota, volvió a lanzarse hacia el área y Rafa Cruz completó su particular triplete. Cinco goles y todavía quedaba casi todo un Mundial por delante. El extremo de Las Palmas, que había encontrado sitio en el once tras la lesión de Imga, estaba convirtiendo su oportunidad en una actuación para recordar. El sexto llegó cuatro minutos después. Ïu Martínez, convertido en un puñal por la banda derecha, volvió a encontrar el camino. Marco Company puso la delicadeza con un toque de seda y Guillermo Trujillano apareció en el área para resolver de primeras. Una combinación de talento, velocidad y precisión. Nada más reanudarse el juego, Trujillano cayó derribado dentro del área, aunque España decidió no solicitar la revisión de una acción que parecía penalti. El marcador ya reflejaba una diferencia abismal. Y todavía no se había alcanzado la media hora. Pero los goles siguieron llegando. En el minuto 35, una mano de Raiyawa permitió a Roberto Tomás completar también su triplete desde los once metros, con un lanzamiento tan sutil como contundente había sido el vendaval anterior. El séptimo. Cinco minutos después, Iu Martínez volvió a levantar la cabeza desde la derecha y puso un centro medido que Trujillano convirtió de cabeza en el octavo. Y cuando el descanso parecía ofrecer al fin algo de misericordia, Marco Company quiso apuntarse a la fiesta. El centrocampista del Real Madrid encontró el hueco para definir con la zurda, abajo, y establecer el noveno antes del mejor momento para Fiyi: el descanso. El entretiempo apenas sirvió para tomar aire. Cubillo movió el banquillo, dio entrada a Mayans y Yeremaiah, que se estrenaba en el Mundial, pero España regresó con el mismo apetito. Dos minutos después de la reanudación, Vata pisó a Ïu Martínez dentro del área y el colegiado señaló penalti. Trujillano asumió la responsabilidad y no perdonó desde los once metros. El décimo. Y apenas dos minutos después llegó el siguiente. Sobral puso el balón en juego desde la esquina y Jorge Domínguez emergió por encima de todos para marcar de cabeza. Ni el paso por vestuarios había conseguido frenar a España. Y Rafa Cruz todavía tenía cuentas pendientes con el gol. En el minuto 56, una recuperación en campo contrario permitió al extremo de Las Palmas aparecer completamente solo por la izquierda y firmar su cuarto tanto de la tarde. Después vinieron casi diez minutos sin marcar. Una eternidad para una España que había convertido cada ataque en una amenaza. Pero el descanso goleador resultó ser un espejismo. Rafa volvió a cazar un balón suelto dentro del área para completar su repóker. El decimocuarto tuvo que esperar hasta el minuto 73. Otro saque de esquina, esta vez botado por Trujillano, encontró nuevamente la cabeza de Jorge Domínguez. El central volvió a hacerse gigante para consumar su doblete. Y todavía faltaba un invitado. Siete minutos después llegó el turno de Yeremaiah. El delantero de La Fábrica, que regresaba tras más de un mes sin competir, llevaba toda la segunda mitad persiguiendo su gol. Lo buscó una y otra vez. Hasta que un disparo de Mayans encontró la punta de su bota y terminó en la red. El decimoquinto y el sello al recreo más largo de la historia.

articles.title: Arsenal boss Arteta eases fears over Raya injury
articles.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said Monday that David Raya's injury was not as bad as first feared after the goalkeeper hurt his shoulder in the weekend draw a...
articles.body:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said Monday that David Raya's injury was not as bad as first feared after the goalkeeper hurt his shoulder in the weekend draw at Newcastle.

The Spaniard was absent from the Gunners' training session on the eve of Tuesday's Champions League match against Bundesliga leaders Borussia Dortmund.

Raya was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga in the 70th minute of the 2-2 draw at St James' Park on Saturday after an apparently innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula.

The 31-year-old left the pitch clutching his left arm in visible discomfort.

"He's not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but he doesn't look too serious," Arteta told his pre-match press conference.

"We need some more tests tomorrow, but it's quite encouraging. With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected."

The Arsenal boss was pushed for more details but said it was too early to say when Raya would be back in action, with a game against Manchester City looming at the weekend.

"There's no need of surgery, which was the main fear, especially because that would rule him out for months, so let's see," he said.

Understudies Arrizabalaga and Frenchman Illan Meslier took part in Monday's training session but Arteta refused to be drawn on who would play against Dortmund at the Emirates.

Raya played a key role as Arsenal ended a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season and had started this campaign with seven clean sheets in 10 matches before the match in Newcastle.

He hurt himself on the day Arsenal welcomed back William Saliba into the matchday squad. The France defender, who was an unused substitute, has not played this season because of an injury.

Winger Bukayo Saka, who has been absent since October 21 due to a thigh injury, is still weeks away from a return.

Arsenal have a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League table and have enjoyed a strong start to the Champions League, winning three of their four games and drawing the other.

articles.title: Arteta delivers 'encouraging' injury update on David Raya ahead of Arsenal match in Champions League
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — David Raya's shoulder injury isn't as serious as initially feared, Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said Monday, but the Spain goalkeeper still req...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — David Raya's shoulder injury isn't as serious as initially feared, Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said Monday, but the Spain goalkeeper still requires further tests to discover the exact nature of the problem.

Raya was in clear pain as he walked off the field midway through the second half of Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Newcastle in the Premier League on Saturday , having hurt himself falling to the ground while jostling with an opponent after catching the ball at a corner kick.

Arteta has provided an update on Raya's condition, saying the goalkeeper would not be available for the Champions League match at home to Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday but that the injury wasn't too serious.

"We need some more tests tomorrow but it's quite encouraging," Arteta said at a news conference. "With the pain he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried. But it seems to be better than we expected."

"There is no need for surgery," Arteta added, "which was the main fear, especially, as that would rule him out for months."

Arteta said Raya "could almost not handle the amount of pain he had" in the seemingly innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula.

"The extent of the pain he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying," he added.

"The first test we have done showed something that is much more encouraging. Tomorrow we need to reaffirm that to be able to give you some more specific information."

articles.title: Pick of the stats: Wolverhampton Wanderers v Derby County
articles.summary: BBC Sport highlights some of the key stats and facts for the Championship match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Derby County.
articles.body:
Wolves will seek to at least keep pace at the top of the Championship when second-bottom Derby visit Molineux on Tuesday (20:00 GMT).

Cesar Peixoto's side are third, a point behind leaders Middlesbrough and second-placed Stoke, after Saturday's 2-1 win over Charlton, which extended their unbeaten run to seven games from which they have earned 17 points.

The Rams are a point off the bottom and five short of safety after going down 2-0 at Southampton on Saturday, their third defeat in four games while they have won just one of 12 games dating back to 1 September.

This is the first league meeting between Wolves and Derby County since the 2017-18 Championship season, when Wolves won both encounters 2-0.

Derby County have failed to score in their past two league games against Wolves, last enduring a longer goalless run against them across three matches in 1979.

Wolves have won just two of their past 11 midweek (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday) league games (D5 L4), including just one of four so far this campaign (D1 L2).

Derby are winless in their past 14 Championship games against sides relegated from the Premier League the previous season (D5 L9) since a 2-1 win over Fulham in April 2022. Their last such away win was in October 2020 at Norwich (1-0).

Wolves' Adam Armstrong has been directly involved in five goals in his past six league appearances against Derby, scoring four and assisting one.

articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund have received a timely boost on the injury front ahead of their upcoming Champions League clash with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.Serhou...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund have received a timely boost on the injury front ahead of their upcoming Champions League clash with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka, who both missed Saturday's 1-0 win over Borussia Mönchengladbach due to muscular injuries, took part in the team's final training session on Monday ahead of Tuesday's encounter.

Meanwhile, Waldemar Anton, who only came off the bench against Gladbach after also struggling with muscular problems, is expected to be fully fit and available for the game in London.

The match is scheduled to kick off at 21:00 CET on Tuesday.
